subject: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking, PrivateLink, IP allowlists
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking, PrivateLink, IP allowlists

Hi Alex —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so your infra and security teams have what they need to evaluate a Private (VPC) deployment: 

Summary of requirements you mentioned
- VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink to avoid public egress for inference traffic
- Static egress IPs / IP allowlist for downstream services
- KMS integration for customer-managed keys
- Audit logs retention for 12 months

Action items we propose
1) Marissa (me) to share a short network diagram and a checklist for peering vs PrivateLink considerations — attached.
2) Alex to confirm preferred connectivity model (VPC Peering vs PrivateLink) and whether you need an on-prem connector for the air-gapped lab.
3) Sean to scope dedicated capacity vs Hosted API fallback SLAs if Dedicated is provisioned behind Private VPC.
4) Vivek to provide IP ranges and suggested firewall rules for egress/ingress.

Attachments: acme-network-diagram.pdf (stub), redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx (stub)

Proposed dates: If you want, we can set up a short 30-min network design session next week with your network/security folks. Tue/Wed mornings PT work well for us.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking, PrivateLink, IP allowlists

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap and the attachments. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Preference: leaning toward AWS PrivateLink to avoid cross-account peering complexity, but our infra lead wants to confirm egress IP behavior for connections to our downstream APIs. Do you provide static egress IPs or a small set of NAT gateway IPs we can allowlist?

2) KMS: we will absolutely need CMK support. Is it possible to bring our own key with the Private deployment (not hosted)?

3) Telemetry: our compliance team requires request-level audit logs for 12 months. Does Redwood support RLS (request-level) and export to our S3 bucket?

4) Availability: we plan a pilot with ~10k requests/day, 95th pct latency target 200ms. If Dedicated capacity is required in the Private VPC, what is the typical lead time to reserve capacity?

Can we do Tue 11/24 10:00am PT for the 30-min network session? Adding Taylor (network infra) to work out details.






— Alex
Product Lead, Acme Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking, PrivateLink, IP allowlists

Alex — thanks, good questions. Short answers below and we can deep-dive on the call Tue 11/24 10am PT. Invite sent.

1) Egress IPs / Allowlist: For PrivateLink we front the interface endpoints from our dedicated managed VPC. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can provide a predictable set of egress IPs via customer-configured NATs or a managed egress pool. I will ask Vivek to include the exact IP ranges and recommended firewall rules in the network session.

2) KMS/CMK: Yes, Customer-Managed Keys are supported for Private deployments. We integrate with AWS KMS and can accept a CMK that you control — we'll share the KMS policy template.

3) Audit logs: We support request-level logging and can stream audit events to your S3. Retention is configurable; 12 months is supported. We'll share the logging schema and sample events ahead of the session.

4) Dedicated capacity lead time: For pilot scale like 10k rps/day, teams typically provision Dedicated within 2-3 weeks once contract is signed. If you need faster, we can discuss burst/fallback on Hosted API while Dedicated is provisioned.

Attachments: network-diagram (updated) referenced in calendar invite.

Sean/Vivek — can you join Tue to cover NAT/egress and capacity sizing?

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking, PrivateLink, IP allowlists

Hi Alex / team — quick pre-call note with the network details we typically need so your firewall and security folks can prepare. We can walk through these on the call but sending in case it helps accelerate: 

Required from Acme before design session:
- Preferred connectivity model: "privatelink" or "vpc-peering" (we recommend PrivateLink for cross-account simplicity)
- CIDR block(s) for the subnets that will host the interface endpoints (if using PrivateLink)
- Any existing NAT/eIP pool you want us to route through, or confirmation you want Redwood-managed egress IPs
- KMS key ARN if you plan to use CMK (we'll provide policy template)
- S3 bucket ARN and cross-account write role to accept audit logs

Redwood deliverables we will bring to the session:
- Example NAT/egress IP ranges for Managed egress (small list for allowlisting)
- KMS policy template and onboarding steps
- Logging schema and example events for request-level audit logs
- A short checklist comparing PrivateLink vs VPC peering (pros/cons)

If you can share CIDR(s) and let us know whether you want our managed egress or to supply eIPs, we can pre-generate a recommended rule set and reduce back-and-forth on the call.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
v.kulkarni@redwood.com
